## Purpose and runtime
Ghostty Config is a browser-based, schema-driven editor that generates minimal Ghostty terminal configuration files, with live visual and terminal previews. It is a Svelte + TypeScript application built by Bun/Vite and deployed to Cloudflare Workers. Deployment configuration is in `wrangler.jsonc`; application shell styling and document setup are in `src/app.html`, `src/app.css`, and `src/routes/+layout.svelte`.

## Entry points and route composition
The landing/editor entry is `src/routes/+page.svelte`, with route initialization in `src/routes/+page.ts`. Settings are category-routed through `src/routes/settings/[category]/+page.svelte`; dedicated workflows exist for keybindings and import/export at `src/routes/settings/keybinds/+page.svelte` and `src/routes/app/import-export/+page.svelte`. Shared layout-level loading belongs in `src/routes/+layout.ts`.

## Typed Ghostty settings model
The core domain boundary is the settings registry: typed option definitions, defaults, metadata, categories, and input semantics are centralized in `src/lib/settings/registry.ts`, `src/lib/settings/options.ts`, and `src/lib/settings/types.ts`. Codecs in `src/lib/settings/codecs.ts` translate between Ghostty config text and typed values; initializers/navigation derive usable editor state and category navigation from this model in `src/lib/settings/initializers.ts` and `src/lib/settings/navigation.ts`.

## State, import/export, and sharing flow
Reactive Svelte stores hold current overrides and app state. `src/lib/stores/config.svelte.ts` is the authoritative editable configuration; it feeds preview components and serialization. `src/lib/stores/import.svelte.ts` imports pasted/uploaded config through codecs, while `src/lib/stores/history.svelte.ts` supports change history. Sharing is URL-oriented serialization logic in `src/lib/utils/share.ts`; modal and toast orchestration are handled by `src/lib/stores/modals.svelte.ts` and `src/lib/stores/toasts.svelte.ts`.

## Schema-driven settings UI
Category pages render registry entries through specialized setting controls under `src/lib/components/settings/`, notably `Item.svelte`, `Group.svelte`, and `KeybindEditor.svelte`. This creates a separation between Ghostty schema/domain types and reusable visual editors. Search state in `src/lib/stores/search.svelte.ts` drives discovery, while `src/lib/components/SettingsSearch.svelte` presents navigation results.

## Preview and terminal subsystem
Live config state is projected into visual previews such as `src/lib/views/InteractiveTerminalDom.svelte`, `src/lib/views/PalettePreview.svelte`, and `src/lib/views/FontPreview.svelte`. The interactive terminal is an in-browser simulation, not a Ghostty process: command dispatch and execution are in `src/lib/terminal/exec.ts` and `src/lib/terminal/commands/index.ts`, backed by a virtual filesystem in `src/lib/terminal/filesystem.ts`. This boundary allows previews to re-theme without invoking external terminal services.

## Generated assets and external upstream inputs
Generated data decouples runtime UI from upstream sources: themes and macOS icons are checked into `src/lib/data/themes.ts` and `src/lib/data/macicons.ts`. Bun scripts fetch upstream Ghostty names/schema and iTerm2 color themes, then regenerate these artifacts: `scripts/generate-ghostty-schema.ts`, `scripts/generate-themes.ts`, and `scripts/generate-macicons.ts`. External dependencies are therefore build/update-time inputs rather than required application backend services.
